clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau raises a question almost nobody asks about cholesterol drugs: do they lower cholesterol? Yes. Do they lower your risk of a heart attack or stroke? According to the data he cites, no.

His bigger concern: those same drugs damage the liver, he says, every time they're taken. He lists what follows - weight gain, hormonal swings, joint and autoimmune trouble - because the liver is one of the body's key organs.

Kevin Trudeau's point isn't to stop any medication on your own. It's to ask your doctor the second question, not just the first: does this lower my risk, or only my number?

What would you ask before your next refill?

#kevintrudeau #cholesterol #hearthealth #healthtruth #wbdaily #askyourdoctor

Kevin Trudeau points out a pattern doctors don't usually explain: cholesterol counts and artery blockages don't always match up.

Some people test at 600 or 700 and live to 90 with no heart disease. Others test very low and still end up with arteries fully blocked. His conclusion: the number alone doesn't tell the whole story.

His view on why the number gets so much weight anyway: it's what sells cholesterol-lowering drugs, prescribed for years at a time.

Kevin Trudeau's point isn't to stop taking anything on your own - it's to ask your doctor what's driving the number, not just what the number says.

What would you ask about your own numbers?
